requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The generator deliberately does not create formatters for types from referenced assemblies (L11), and this change adds an explicit opt-in path for them via the attribute. This is consistent with L11 because it does not change the default TypeCollector behaviour.

findings.claim: The contractless field filter is inverted. `IsPublicReadWrite` accepts a field only when `field.IsReadOnly` is true. A public mutable field of T (e.g. `public int Counter;`) is therefore never serialized, which breaks 'contractless behaviour over public members'. A public `readonly` field is selected instead. `CreateMember` hard-codes `IsWritable: true`, so the generated Deserialize assigns to the readonly field and Project B fails to compile (CS0191). The same filter makes surrogate keys that name a mutable field report MsgPack022.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterContractlessRulesTests.PublicMutableFieldIsSerializedAndReadonlyFieldDoesNotBreakBuild. Expected on head: '.Counter' is missing from the generated source and/or CS0191 is reported. A mutant changing `field.IsReadOnly` to `!field.IsReadOnly` makes the test pass.

findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored, although the acceptance criteria require them to be honoured. With no surrogate, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`, which uses string keys by member name. It never checks T for `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` or `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]`. A T in a referenced assembly with `[MessagePackObject]` and `[Key(0)]`, `[Key(1)]` therefore gets a map formatter keyed by name instead of the array layout its attributes define. `[IgnoreMember]` members are serialized anyway.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterContractlessRulesTests.MessagePackAttributesOnFormattedTypeAreHonoured. Expected on head: the generated formatter uses WriteMapHeader rather than WriteArrayHeader and still serializes the [IgnoreMember] member.

findings.claim: The contractless field filter is inverted. `IsPublicReadWrite` accepts an `IFieldSymbol` only when `field.IsReadOnly` is true. As a result, ordinary mutable public fields (`public int X;`) are never serialized, which breaks the documented and required 'every public read-write instance property and field'. This hits structs and DTOs from referenced assemblies that expose plain fields: they silently produce empty or partial payloads, so data is lost on round-trip.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterFieldSelectionTests.MutablePublicFieldIsSerialized. The data type has a public read-write field `MutableFieldMarker`, and the generated sources do not contain it on head.

findings.claim: The same inverted check selects `public readonly` fields as serializable members. `CreateMember` then marks them `IsWritable: true`, so the generated Deserialize assigns to a readonly field. The result is CS0191 in generated code, which breaks the user's build. In surrogate mode, a surrogate `[Key]` member that names a public readonly field also passes `IsPublicReadWrite` and causes the same compile error, while a matching mutable field is rejected with MsgPack022.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterFieldSelectionTests.ReadonlyPublicFieldIsNotAssigned. The output compilation contains CS0191 and the generated text references `ReadonlyFieldMarker`.

hunches.claim: In surrogate mode, every instance field and property of the surrogate must carry `[Key]` or `[IgnoreMember]`, including private and protected members, because `GetInstanceMembers` does not filter by accessibility. A surrogate with a private helper field, or a non-public property without `[Key]`, is rejected with MsgPack004. That is stricter than MsgPack004's contract, which per L5 applies only to public members.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a surrogate class with `[Key(0)] public int A { get; set; }` plus `private int helper;`, where T has a public `A` property. Run the generator and expect no MsgPack004. On head, MsgPack004 is reported on `helper` and no formatter is generated.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode serializes only public read-write members. For fields, IsPublicReadWrite requires field.IsReadOnly, so it keeps only readonly fields and excludes normal mutable public fields. The doc comment says public read-write fields are serialized, so this looks like an inverted condition. Ordinary public fields would be silently omitted from the wire format.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for `class T { public int F; public int P {get;set;} }` and serialize it. Expect keys F and P; currently F is missing. Also try `public readonly int R`, which would be wrongly included and cannot be assigned on deserialize.

hunches.claim: A new GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect call and the contractless member ordering (alphabetical ordinal) differ from ContractlessStandardResolver, which orders members by declaration order. This changes the map key order on the wire, so bytes are not identical to dynamic contractless output. Readers match keys, so it is mostly interoperable, but the bytes differ.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize `class T { public int Z{get;set;} public int A{get;set;} }` with ContractlessStandardResolver and with the generated formatter, then compare the bytes.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode silently drops public get-only properties and readonly fields, and the field check in IsPublicReadWrite is inverted: it requires field.IsReadOnly, so writable public fields are excluded and only readonly fields are selected. Generated deserialization code would then assign to readonly fields, which fails compilation, or members are silently missing. This is a correctness bug rather than a security issue, but selecting the wrong members changes what data crosses the wire (fields intended to be serialized are skipped, unintended ones included). Note that MessagePackSecurity (UntrustedData) handling is unaffected because the generated body uses the standard templates.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot or generator test: a referenced-assembly type with `public int F;` (writable field) and `public readonly int R;`, annotated formatter in the consuming assembly. Assert the generated formatter includes F, excludes R, and the output compiles.

hunches.claim: The README documents contractless mode as serializing 'public, read-write' members and skipping read-only ones. The ledger records no decision on this: L19 says 'no preference; follow the requirement'. The requirement says the formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members and honours MessagePack attributes on T when they exist. The change ignores [MessagePackObject]/[Key] on T, so the surrogate is the only way to customise keys.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] members (in an assembly referencing MessagePack), plus a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for it. Assert the generated bytes use array/int keys. This is expected to fail because contractless string-key mode is always used.

hunches.claim: The new Msgpack019-022 diagnostics are emitted from the generator via RegisterSourceOutput, but the analyzer only declares them in SupportedDiagnostics and has no analysis action for them. Also, the docs say the 'Generated formatter must be partial' check applies to nesting types, but IsPartial inspects only the formatter class itself, not its containing types. A non-partial nesting type is not diagnosed under MsgPack019.

receipt_plan.detail: Declare a partial formatter nested in a non-partial outer class; expect MsgPack019 per doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md and assert it is reported.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite accepts a public readonly field (`field.IsReadOnly`) instead of excluding it, so contractless mode treats readonly fields as writable. The generated deserializer would assign to a readonly field, which fails to compile or is wrong. No test covers a type with a readonly field.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:268 swap-boolean: `field.IsReadOnly` -> `!field.IsReadOnly`; expected to survive because no ExternalTypes type declares any public field, so no test exercises the field branch.

hunches.claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured. The collector ignores T's attributes ([Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract]) entirely, and no test uses an attributed T. The ExternalTypes assembly has no MessagePack reference, so it cannot cover this.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator test where T has [MessagePackObject]/[Key] attributes with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class, and assert the generated keys follow the attributes. Currently it would fail because contractless keys are generated.

hunches.claim: The surrogate path is only covered for integer keys with a gap, and for error cases. Nothing tests string-key surrogates, duplicate keys (KeysMustBeUnique), or a surrogate member missing [Key] (MemberNeedsKey). Deleting the claimedKeys check or the key-kind guard would survive. The mixed-key test expects MsgPack005 from the analyzer path, not from the generator path.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:176 delete-statement: remove the `if (!claimedKeys.Add(key))` block; expected to survive because no test has duplicate surrogate keys.

hunches.claim: Diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are tested, but the diagnostic tests do not cover the generation-time guards: NoDeserializingConstructor for a class without a parameterless constructor, inaccessible T, and a generic T. Removing the constructor guard or the IsGenericType check would not fail any test.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:75 remove-guard: delete the `isClass && !...InstanceConstructors.Any(...)` block; expected to survive because no test formats a class without a public parameterless constructor.

hunches.claim: The GeneratorUtilities filter that excludes [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from hand-written formatter registration has no direct test. The registration test would only notice a duplicate if it caused a compile error or a wrong type, and the mutant is likely to survive.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: delete the `!symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...)` clause; run the ExecutionTests and the generator snapshot tests.

hunches.claim: The string-key and int-key template changes (the IsUserDeclaredFormatter ternary) are exercised only by execution tests. No generator snapshot test checks the emitted `partial class` text or that the `internal sealed class` path still works for existing types. Test coverage for the template branch is indirect.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests and check that no existing snapshot changed. Also add a snapshot for a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class.

hunches.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration. A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F` nested inside a non-partial containing type gets no MsgPack019. The generator still emits the nesting wrappers through `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces`, which yields CS0260/CS0101 in generated code instead of a clear diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: IsPartial (lines 291-297) inspects only `symbol.DeclaringSyntaxReferences` of the formatter, not `ContainingType` chain; compare with MsgPack011 handling for nested [MessagePackObject] types in TypeCollector.

hunches.claim: The new MsgPack019-022 descriptors are added to SupportedDiagnostics, but GeneratedFormatterCollector reports them through the source generator's RegisterSourceOutput. They are only enabled for [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] users, so existing users are not affected. However, the rows may be missing from AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md. If so, RS2008 would fire in the analyzer project, and warnings-as-errors would break the build for contributors. The hunks do not show this file, so this is unverified.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md lists MsgPack019-022; build the analyzer project and look for RS2000/RS2008.

hunches.claim: The new GeneratedFormatterCollector is not run during normal analysis. It is only wired into the generator pipeline, which means MsgPack019-022 are reported only when the generator runs. A hand-written class that implements IMessagePackFormatter<T> and carries the attribute is now skipped by the hand-written-formatter registration in GeneratorUtilities. If the collector then rejects it (non-partial, or a generic T), the class is silently dropped from the generated resolver and only a diagnostic remains. This is only reachable for classes that already use the new attribute, so existing users are not affected.

receipt_plan.detail: Read GeneratorUtilities.cs:35 and the generatedFormatterDiagnostics path in MessagePackGenerator.cs.

hunches.claim: The generator pipeline passes reportDiagnostic: null to Collect and the diagnostics path is separate. In the diagnostics path, if ReferenceSymbols.TryCreate fails, no diagnostics are reported, so a misconfigured [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] is silently ignored. This is a minor reliability issue with no direct protection being disabled.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the generatedFormatterDiagnostics SelectMany: when ReferenceSymbols.TryCreate returns false, it returns an empty array with no diagnostic.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour over public members' means only public read-write instance properties and fields, string-keyed by name. Read-only members are skipped and deserialization needs an accessible parameterless constructor (any struct qualifies). This is what GeneratedFormatterCollector.CreateContractlessMembers plus the NoDeserializingConstructor check implement.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour' means matching ContractlessStandardResolver. Public get-only properties and readonly fields are also serialized: IsPublicReadWrite becomes IsPublicReadable for the member list, with IsWritable set per member. Deserialization picks a public constructor whose parameters match member names and types and passes them as constructorParameters to ObjectSerializationInfo.Create, instead of always requiring a parameterless constructor.
